skill_drafts.name: Configure Maven for Reproducible Builds
skill_drafts.description: Set up Maven build configuration to ensure consistent, reproducible output across different environments and build runs. Use when standardizing build artifacts for distribution or compliance.
applicable_signals: Multiple environments must produce identical artifacts
Compliance or audit requirements demand reproducible builds
contraindications: Debugging single-run builds where environment variation aids diagnosis
Build environment-specific variation is intentional or required
Rapid prototyping where build consistency is not a priority
workflow_steps: Review current Maven pom.xml and settings.xml for environment-dependent properties
Document all build parameters: compiler version, plugin versions, dependency versions, timestamps
Configure reproducible build properties in pom.xml (e.g., project.build.outputTimestamp)
Update settings.xml to enforce consistent repository mirrors and credentials handling
Execute build in first environment and capture artifact checksums
Execute build in second environment and verify artifact checksums match
Document reproducible build configuration and validation results
triggers: Initiating a new Maven project requiring build consistency
Enforcing build consistency across CI/CD pipelines
Preparing artifacts for release or distribution
constraints: All build properties must be explicitly declared in pom.xml or settings.xml
Build output must be validated across at least two independent runs
cautions: Reproducible build configuration may conflict with dynamic dependency resolution; pin versions explicitly
Timestamp and build metadata must be controlled to avoid non-deterministic output
output_contract: Maven configuration (pom.xml, settings.xml) with reproducible build properties documented and validated across test runs. Artifacts produced in different environments must have identical checksums.

metadata.prompt: Configure Maven pom.xml and settings.xml with reproducible build properties. Document and validate configuration across multiple test runs to confirm consistency. Ensure build output is identical regardless of build environment or execution time.

skill_drafts.name: Configure Maven Classloading and Module Dependencies
skill_drafts.description: Manage Maven classloading behavior and multi-module project structure to resolve dependency conflicts and ensure correct class resolution across module boundaries.
skill_drafts.objective: Resolve classloading and multi-module dependency issues
applicable_signals: Multiple pom.xml files in project hierarchy
contraindications: Single-module projects with no dependency conflicts
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': "Define parent pom.xml with packaging type 'pom' and list all child modules"}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Create dependencyManagement section in parent pom to centralize version declarations'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Configure each child module pom.xml with parent reference and explicit dependencies'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify classloading order by running mvn dependency:tree to inspect resolved versions'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Test multi-module build with mvn clean install to confirm no ClassNotFoundException'}
constraints: Parent pom must be defined before child modules reference it
Dependency management section must precede actual dependency declarations
Module order in parent pom affects build sequence
cautions: Circular module dependencies will cause build failure
Overriding parent dependency versions in child modules can cause unexpected behavior
Classloader isolation may hide transitive dependency issues
output_contract: Multi-module pom.xml structure with correct parent-child relationships, centralized dependency management section, and verified classloading order confirmed via dependency tree output and successful build execution.

metadata.prompt: When working with multi-module Maven builds, configure parent-child pom relationships, define dependency management sections, and verify classloading order to prevent ClassNotFoundException and version conflicts. Ensure each module declares its dependencies explicitly and parent pom centralizes version management.

skill_drafts.name: Build Maven Project for Multiple Environments
skill_drafts.description: Configure Maven profiles and toolchains to build and package applications for different target environments (dev, staging, production). Use when deploying to heterogeneous infrastructure or requiring environment-specific binaries.
contraindications: Environment differences handled at runtime only
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Define Maven profiles in pom.xml', 'detail': 'Create <profile> blocks for each environment (dev, staging, production) with environment-specific properties and plugin configurations'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure toolchains.xml', 'detail': 'Map tool versions (JDK, compiler, etc.) per environment to ensure consistent build tooling'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Activate profile during build', 'detail': 'Use -P flag (mvn clean package -P production) or settings.xml activation rules'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Validate generated artifacts', 'detail': 'Verify that artifacts contain correct environment-specific configurations'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Test in target environment', 'detail': 'Deploy and test artifacts in their intended environment before release'}
constraints: Profiles must be defined in pom.xml or settings.xml
Toolchains.xml must exist and be properly configured
Profile activation must be explicit or rule-based
cautions: Ensure profile names are consistent across CI/CD and local builds
Validate toolchain availability on all build agents
Test artifacts in target environment before production release
output_contract: Maven profiles and toolchain configuration (toolchains.xml) producing validated artifacts for each target environment, with confirmed environment-specific properties embedded in each artifact

metadata.prompt:
1. Define Maven profiles in pom.xml for each target environment, specifying environment-specific properties, dependencies, and plugin configurations.
2. Create or update toolchains.xml to map tool versions (compiler, JDK, etc.) per environment.
3. Activate the appropriate profile during build using -P flag or settings.xml activation rules.
4. Validate that the generated artifacts (JAR, WAR, etc.) contain correct environment-specific configurations.
5. Test artifacts in their target environment to confirm correctness before release.
